Then those brahmins, enraged upon seeing him in the form of a rogue / holding a human skull, all reviled him with cries of “Fie!”
“Again and again, sinner, sinner! Begone, begone, lowest of men! / For the sacrificial altar is not fit for you, a bearer of human bones!”
Then, laughing heartily, the Lord threw the skull / onto the sacrificial altar, O ruler of the gods, and vanished; he was not recognized by the wise men.
When he had vanished, that skull was thrown outside the pavilion; / but then another of identical form appeared there, O fair-faced one.
As often as it was thrown away, another appeared there upon the earth: / thus hundreds of thousands, millions, and tens of millions.
As [many] were thrown there, so many were produced. Filled with astonishment at that, / all the sages, despondent at his deed, then said:

16.103.s:
ko'nyo devānmahādevādgaṃgākṣālitaśekharāt ..
samartha īdṛśaṃ karttumasminyajñe viśeṣataḥ .. 7.1.103.10 ..
tataste vi vidhaiḥ stotraiḥ stuvaṃto vṛṣabhadhvajam ..
homaṃ cakrurmuhurvahnau maṃtraistaiḥ śatarudriyaiḥ .. 11 ..
tataḥ pratyakṣatāṃ prāptasteṣāṃ devo maheśvaraḥ ..
tataste vividhaiḥ stotraistuṣṭuvuḥ śūlapāṇinam..
vedoktamaṃtrairvividhaiḥ purāṇoktaistathaiva ca .. 12 ..
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
oṃ namo mūlaprakṛtaye ajitāya mahātmane ..
anāvṛtāya devāya niḥspṛhāya namonamaḥ .. 13 ..
nama ādyāya bījāya ārṣeyāya pravarttine ..
anaṃtarāya caikāya avyaktāya namonamaḥ .. ... 14 ..
nānāvicitrabhujagāṃgadabhūṣaṇāya sarveśvarāya virajāya namo varāya ..
viśvātmane paramakāraṇakāraṇāya phullāraviṃdavipulāyatalocanāya .. .. 15 ..
16.103.d:
कोऽन्यो देवान्महादेवाद्गंगाक्षालितशेखरात् ..
समर्थ ईदृशं कर्त्तुमस्मिन्यज्ञे विशेषतः .. 7.1.103.10 ..
ततस्ते वि विधैः स्तोत्रैः स्तुवंतो वृषभध्वजम् ..
होमं चक्रुर्मुहुर्वह्नौ मंत्रैस्तैः शतरुद्रियैः .. 11 ..
ततः प्रत्यक्षतां प्राप्तस्तेषां देवो महेश्वरः ..
ततस्ते विविधैः स्तोत्रैस्तुष्टुवुः शूलपाणिनम्..
वेदोक्तमंत्रैर्विविधैः पुराणोक्तैस्तथैव च .. 12 ..
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
ओं नमो मूलप्रकृतये अजिताय महात्मने ..
अनावृताय देवाय निःस्पृहाय नमोनमः .. 13 ..
नम आद्याय बीजाय आर्षेयाय प्रवर्त्तिने ..
अनंतराय चैकाय अव्यक्ताय नमोनमः .. ... 14 ..
नानाविचित्रभुजगांगदभूषणाय सर्वेश्वराय विरजाय नमो वराय ..
विश्वात्मने परमकारणकारणाय फुल्लारविंदविपुलायतलोचनाय .. .. 15 ..
16.103.m:
“Who other than the god Mahādeva, whose crest is washed by the Gaṅgā, / is capable of doing such a thing, especially at this sacrifice?”
Then, praising the one whose banner bears a bull with various hymns of praise, / they repeatedly performed oblations into the fire with the Śatarudrīya mantras.
Then the god Maheśvara became visible before their eyes. / Thereupon they praised the trident-bearing Lord with various hymns of praise, / with diverse mantras taught in the Vedas, and likewise with those taught in the Purāṇas.
The seers said: / “Oṃ, homage to the primal nature, to the unconquered Great Self, / to the unobstructed god, to the desireless one, homage, homage!
Homage to the first seed, the source of the seers, the impeller, / to the endless, the one, the unmanifest, homage, homage!
Homage to the supreme one, adorned with diverse, wondrous serpent-armlets, Lord of all, free from passion, / the Self of the universe, the cause of the supreme cause, whose wide, expansive eyes are like blooming lotuses!

16.103.s:
adṛśyamavyaktamanādimavyayaṃ yadakṣaraṃ brahma vadaṃti sarvagam ..
niśāmya yaṃ mṛtyumukhātpramucyate tamādidevaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye .. 16 ..
evaṃ stutastadā sarvairṛṣibhirgatakalmaṣaiḥ ..
tatastuṣṭo mahādevasteṣāṃ pratyakṣatāṃ gataḥ ..
abravīttānṛṣīndevo vṛṇudhvaṃ varamuttamam .. 17 ..
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
yadi tuṣṭo'si no deva sthāne'sminnirato bhava ..
asaṃkhyātāni yasmācca kapālāni sureśvara .. 18 ..
punaḥ punaḥ pravṛttāni vyapanītānyapi prabho ..
asminnasaṃśayaṃ sthāne kapāleśvaranāmabhṛt.. 19 ..
svayaṃ tu liṃgaṃ deveśa tiṣṭhenmanvaṃtarāṃtaram ..
kapāleśvaranāmnā tvamasminsthāne sthitiṃ kuru.. 7.1.103.20 ..
yetra tvāṃ pūjayiṣyaṃti dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
teṣāṃ tu paramaṃ sthānaṃ yaddevairapi durlabham .. 21 ..
16.103.d:
अदृश्यमव्यक्तमनादिमव्ययं यदक्षरं ब्रह्म वदंति सर्वगम् ..
निशाम्य यं मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुच्यते तमादिदेवं शरणं प्रपद्ये .. 16 ..
एवं स्तुतस्तदा सर्वैरृषिभिर्गतकल्मषैः ..
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवस्तेषां प्रत्यक्षतां गतः ..
अब्रवीत्तानृषीन्देवो वृणुध्वं वरमुत्तमम् .. 17 ..
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
यदि तुष्टोऽसि नो देव स्थानेऽस्मिन्निरतो भव ..
असंख्यातानि यस्माच्च कपालानि सुरेश्वर .. 18 ..
पुनः पुनः प्रवृत्तानि व्यपनीतान्यपि प्रभो ..
अस्मिन्नसंशयं स्थाने कपालेश्वरनामभृत्.. 19 ..
स्वयं तु लिंगं देवेश तिष्ठेन्मन्वंतरांतरम् ..
कपालेश्वरनाम्ना त्वमस्मिन्स्थाने स्थितिं कुरु.. 7.1.103.20 ..
येत्र त्वां पूजयिष्यंति धूपमाल्यानुलेपनैः ..
तेषां तु परमं स्थानं यद्देवैरपि दुर्लभम् .. 21 ..
16.103.m:
That which they declare to be the unseeable, unmanifest, beginningless, imperishable, indestructible, all-pervading Brahman, / having perceived which one is freed from the jaws of death—in that primeval god I take refuge.”
Thus praised then by all the sinless seers, / Mahādeva, pleased thereby, appeared before their eyes / and the god said to those seers: “Choose an excellent boon!”
The brahmins said: / “If you are pleased with us, O God, remain devoted to this place, / since countless skulls, O ruler of the gods,
appeared again and again, even when removed, O Lord. / Without doubt, in this place, bearing the name Kapāleśvara,
may your liṅga remain self-manifest, O Lord of gods, until another manvantara; / make your abode in this place under the name Kapāleśvara.
Those who will worship you here with incense, garlands, and ointments— / for them shall be the supreme abode, which is hard even for the gods to attain.”

16.103.s:
bāḍhamityevamuktvā'sau sthita statramaheśvaraḥ ..
punaḥ pravartito yajño niśānāthasya bhāmini .. 22 ..
tasmindṛṣṭe labhenmartyo vājimedhaphalaṃ priye ..
mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ pūrva janmārjjitairapi .. 23 ..
idaṃ māhātmyamakhilamabhūtsvāyaṃbhuvāṃtare ..
vaivasvate punaścānyaddakṣayajñavināśakṛt .. 24 ..
kapālīti maheśāno dakṣeṇoktaḥ purā haraḥ ..
tena yajñasya vidhvaṃsaṃ kapālī tamathākarot ..
kapāleśvaranāmeti sthitosminmānavāntare .. 25 ..
athāsya nāma devasya sūrya sāvarṇikeṃ'tare ..
bhaviṣyati varārohe nāma tattveśvareti ca .. 26 ..
iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ rudradaivatam..
pāpaghnaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ paśupāśavimokṣaṇam .. 27 ..
16.103.d:
बाढमित्येवमुक्त्वाऽसौ स्थित स्तत्रमहेश्वरः ..
पुनः प्रवर्तितो यज्ञो निशानाथस्य भामिनि .. 22 ..
तस्मिन्दृष्टे लभेन्मर्त्यो वाजिमेधफलं प्रिये ..
मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैः पूर्व जन्मार्ज्जितैरपि .. 23 ..
इदं माहात्म्यमखिलमभूत्स्वायंभुवांतरे ..
वैवस्वते पुनश्चान्यद्दक्षयज्ञविनाशकृत् .. 24 ..
कपालीति महेशानो दक्षेणोक्तः पुरा हरः ..
तेन यज्ञस्य विध्वंसं कपाली तमथाकरोत् ..
कपालेश्वरनामेति स्थितोस्मिन्मानवान्तरे .. 25 ..
अथास्य नाम देवस्य सूर्य सावर्णिकेंऽतरे ..
भविष्यति वरारोहे नाम तत्त्वेश्वरेति च .. 26 ..
इति संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं माहात्म्यं रुद्रदैवतम्..
पापघ्नं सर्वजंतूनां पशुपाशविमोक्षणम् .. 27 ..
16.103.m:
Saying, “So be it,” Maheśvara remained there. / And the sacrifice of the lord of the night was resumed, O passionate lady.
When it is beheld, a mortal obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice, O dear one, / and is freed from all sins, even those accumulated in previous births.
This entire māhātmya occurred in the Svāyambhuva manvantara. / But in the Vaivasvata manvantara there was another, which brought about the destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice.
Formerly, Maheśāna Hara was called ‘Kapālī’ by Dakṣa; / on account of that, Kapālī then destroyed his sacrifice. / Under the name Kapāleśvara he has remained in this manvantara.
Then, in the Sūryasāvarṇika manvantara, the name of this god / will be Tattveśvara, O fair-hipped lady.
Thus has been declared in brief the māhātmya whose deity is Rudra, / which destroys the sins of all living beings and brings release from the snare of the beast.

16.103.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye madhyayātrāyāṃ kapāleśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma tryadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 103 ..
16.103.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये मध्ययात्रायां कपालेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्र्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः .. 103 ..
16.103.m: Thus ends the one hundred and third chapter, entitled ‘The Description of the Māhātmya of Kapāleśvara’ in the Middle Pilgrimage, in the first section, the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, in the seventh book, Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

16.104.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi koṭīśvaramanuttamam ..
tasmāduttarato devi koṭīśamiti viśrutam .. 1 ..
16.104.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि कोटीश्वरमनुत्तमम् ..
तस्मादुत्तरतो देवि कोटीशमिति विश्रुतम् .. 1 ..
16.104.m: Īśvara said: / “Then one should go, O great goddess, to the unsurpassed Koṭīśvara; / to the north of that, O goddess, is the one renowned as Koṭīśa,

16.104.s:
pāpaghnaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ paśupāśavimokṣadam ..
purā pāśupatā devi kapāleśvarasaṃnidhau .. 2 ..
16.104.d:
पापघ्नं सर्वजंतूनां पशुपाशविमोक्षदम् ..
पुरा पाशुपता देवि कपालेश्वरसंनिधौ .. 2 ..
16.104.m: which destroys the sins of all living beings and grants release from the snare of the beast. / Formerly, O goddess, Pāśupatas in the presence of Kapāleśvara

16.104.s:
tapaḥ kurvaṃti vipulaṃ bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ ..
jaṭāmukuṭasaṃyuktā muṃjamekhaladhāriṇaḥ .. 3 ..
16.104.d:
तपः कुर्वंति विपुलं भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहाः ..
जटामुकुटसंयुक्ता मुंजमेखलधारिणः .. 3 ..
16.104.m: performed extensive austerity, their bodies smeared with ashes, / bearing crowns of matted locks and wearing girdles of muñja grass,

16.104.s:
śāṃtāḥ sarve jitakrodhā brāhmaṇāḥ śivayoginaḥ ..
tapaḥ kurvaṃti tatrasthā vyāpya kṣetraṃ caturddiśam .. 4 ..
16.104.d:
शांताः सर्वे जितक्रोधा ब्राह्मणाः शिवयोगिनः ..
तपः कुर्वंति तत्रस्था व्याप्य क्षेत्रं चतुर्द्दिशम् .. 4 ..
16.104.m: all tranquil, having conquered anger, brahmins who were Śiva-yogins. / Staying there, they performed austerity, occupying the sacred field on all four sides,

16.104.s:
koṭisaṃkhyā mahādevi mantrajāpyaparāyaṇāḥ ..
samyaksaṃsthāpya te liṃgaṃ kapāleśasamīpagam .. 5 ..
16.104.d:
कोटिसंख्या महादेवि मन्त्रजाप्यपरायणाः ..
सम्यक्संस्थाप्य ते लिंगं कपालेशसमीपगम् .. 5 ..
16.104.m: a crore in number, O great goddess, devoted to the muttering of mantras. / Having properly established a liṅga near Kapāleśa,

16.104.s:
tataste pūjayāṃcakrustalliṃgaṃ bhaktisaṃyutāḥ ..
tatastuṣṭo mahādevo muktiṃ teṣāṃ dadau haraḥ .. 6 ..
16.104.d:
ततस्ते पूजयांचक्रुस्तल्लिंगं भक्तिसंयुताः ..
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवो मुक्तिं तेषां ददौ हरः .. 6 ..
16.104.m: they then worshipped that liṅga with devotion. / Pleased with that, Mahādeva Hara granted them liberation.

16.104.s:
ṛṣayaḥ koṭisaṃkhyātāstasminsiddhā yataḥ priye ..
tena koṭīśvaraṃ liṃgaṃ nāmnā khyātaṃ dharātale .. 7 ..
16.104.d:
ऋषयः कोटिसंख्यातास्तस्मिन्सिद्धा यतः प्रिये ..
तेन कोटीश्वरं लिंगं नाम्ना ख्यातं धरातले .. 7 ..
16.104.m: Since seers numbering a crore attained perfection there, O dear one, / therefore that liṅga became famed on earth by the name Koṭīśvara.

16.104.s:
yastaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā koṭīśvaramanāmayam ..
sa koṭimantrajāpyasya phalaṃ prāpsyati mānavaḥ .. 8 ..
16.104.d:
यस्तं पूजयते भक्त्या कोटीश्वरमनामयम् ..
स कोटिमन्त्रजाप्यस्य फलं प्राप्स्यति मानवः .. 8 ..
16.104.m: A person who worships that faultless Koṭīśvara with devotion / shall obtain the fruit of muttering a mantra a crore of times.

16.104.s:
hiraṇyaṃ tatra dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇe vedapārage ..
koṭihomaphalaṃ tasya samyagyātrāphalaṃ bhavet .. 9 ..
16.104.d:
हिरण्यं तत्र दातव्यं ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे ..
कोटिहोमफलं तस्य सम्यग्यात्राफलं भवेत् .. 9 ..
16.104.m: Gold should be given there to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas; / his fruit of a proper pilgrimage shall be the fruit of a crore of fire-oblations.”

16.104.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye koṭīśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma caturadhika śatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 104 ..
16.104.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये कोटीश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम चतुरधिक शततमोऽध्यायः .. 104 ..
16.104.m: Thus ends the one hundred and fourth chapter, entitled ‘The Description of the Māhātmya of Koṭīśvara’ in the first section, the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, in the seventh book, Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
